spec.full_target:
Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with the standing definitions of Section 2 of the supplied paper.

Use normalized measure dx/(2*pi) on the torus \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/(2*pi \mathbb{Z}). The Fourier coefficient is
\hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx,
and ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2s)|\hat f(k)|^2, where <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2).
These spaces are the completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms; negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. The normalized L^2 norm is the s=0 norm. For mean-zero functions, the homogeneous norm uses |k|^(2s) in place of <k>^(2s). For s>=0,
||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s);
for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s).
Real-valued means \hat f(-k)=overline(\hat f(k)), and mean-zero means \hat f(0)=0.
All time suprema concern continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

Let S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), so \widehat{S_t f}(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)\hat f(k).
Let P_0 be the mean and P=I-P_0. Let D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at k=0; D^(-2)=(D^(-1))^2.
The equation is
u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2),  u(0)=u_0. [Eq. (1)]
The exact solution u is the unique real, mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation and satisfies this equation distributionally.

For a positive integer L and tau=T/L, the fixed time-semidiscrete scheme is u^0=u_0 and
u^(n+1)=S_tau u^n+F_tau(u^n)+H_tau(u^n), 0<=n<L, [Eq. (2)]
where
F_tau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(D^(-1)f)^2],
H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
This is the fixed scheme of the paper's reference [1, Eq. (1.4)], without a spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, every 0<gamma<=1 and every R>0, there exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real, mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(\mathbb{T}) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau_0, this exact fixed scheme satisfies
max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2)<=C*tau^gamma.
The same C and tau_0 apply to the entire stated initial-data ball; no spectral support bound or additional smoothness is a hypothesis.

In the source's standing notation v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) and M=1+sup_(0<=t<=T)||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
Constants C_M may vary from line to line and depend on gamma,T,M, but are uniform in n,tau and spectral support. Section 2.1 supplies M<=1+A(T,gamma,R) uniformly on the ball using the cited exact-flow results; it is not an extra hypothesis on u_0. The source uses the continuous estimates from [1, Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 7.2] and does not use the logarithmic convergence theorem as an input.
spec.conclusion: There exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer Lsteps with tau=T/Lsteps<=tau_0, the exact solution of KdV(u;u_0) exists with the stipulated smooth-approximation meaning and the unfiltered recursion u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) satisfies max_(0<=n<=Lsteps)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. Both constants are uniform on the entire initial-data ball and independent of Fourier support and additional smoothness.

propositions.statement: 0<gamma<=1.

For the real mean-zero periodic equation U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx on R/(2*pi*Z), use hat U(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral U(x)exp(-i*k*x)dx, ||U||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2s)|hat U(k)|^2, and z_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t)hat U(t)(k). For every s>0 and horizon Q>0, every initial datum U_0 in dot H^s has a distributional solution with z in C([0,Q];dot H^s), unique in the source solution class (z in L^infinity dot H^0 satisfying z_k(t)-z_k(0)=(i*k/2)integral_0^t sum_(k1+k2=k)exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*r)z_k1(r)z_k2(r)dr). Its dot H^0 norm is conserved, and the flow depends Lipschitz continuously on the initial data in dot H^s, uniformly on bounded dot H^s sets on [0,Q]. The Galerkin approximations (with the nonlinear inputs and output projected to |k|<=m and high coefficients frozen) have dot H^s bounds uniform in m, depending only on s,Q, the initial dot H^s norm and an upper bound for the initial dot H^0 norm. For 0<sigma<s they admit a subsequence converging strongly in L^q([0,Q];dot H^sigma), 1<q<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s to this solution; the same dot H^s bound holds for the limit. For s=0 there is a unique C([0,Q];dot H^0) solution, conserving that norm and depending Lipschitz continuously on its data. These flows agree on overlapping regularity classes and are obtained by smooth approximation.

argument.text: H001-H003 give T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. Fix a0 and temporarily assume L1: a0 is real, mean-zero, in H^gamma and ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R. Set U0(x)=-a0(-x), so hat U0(k)=-hat a0(-k). It is real and mean-zero and preserves all Fourier Sobolev norms. In particular ||U0||_(dot H^gamma)<=R and ||U0||_2<=R. Apply E001 with s=gamma,Q=T,U_0=U0. Its hypotheses hold by these norm facts and H001-H002. It supplies a unique continuous source flow U, a uniform homogeneous bound depending only on T,gamma,R, and smooth-approximation construction. Record its existence as F001.

produces.statement: There exists the unique source solution with initial datum U0 on [0,T], continuous in dot H^gamma, bounded there by a constant depending only on T,gamma,R, constructed by smooth approximation.

argument.text: Choose U from F001 and set u(t,x)=-U(t,-x). For smooth solutions u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx at (t,-x), so u_t+u_xxx=-UU_x=u*u_x=(1/2)partial_x(u^2). The same equality follows distributionally by the reflection change of variables for the limiting solution. Fourier coefficients satisfy hat u(t)(k)=-hat U(t)(-k), hence all Sobolev norms, zero mean and reality are preserved. The comparison ||u||_(H^gamma)<=2^(gamma/2)||U||_(dot H^gamma) gives a bound A(T,gamma,R). Finite Fourier norm sums pass to the limit under smooth approximation, and their supremum gives the full bound; continuity gives it for every time. Uniqueness follows by applying the inverse reflection to two solutions, using the source coefficient formulation, equivalent to the distributional equation for continuous L^2 paths by testing each Fourier mode. Set v=S_(-t)u. Unit-modulus multipliers preserve its H^gamma norm. Differentiation for smooth data gives v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v).

produces.statement: Under L1 the exact u exists uniquely, sup_[0,T]||u||_(H^gamma)<=A(T,gamma,R), v=S_(-t)u has the same bound, and for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v).

argument.text: For the smooth-data clause, temporarily assume L3: a0 is smooth. Apply E001 at every positive integer regularity s, with this same U0. Its finite higher norms and uniqueness make all these solutions coincide with U. Thus u is spatially smooth, and the equation supplies its time smoothness. Discharge L3 to obtain that conditional clause, and discharge L1 to obtain the stated assertion for every a0 in the ball. For the pairwise assertion fix arbitrary a0,b0 and temporarily assume L2: they are real mean-zero L^2 data whose norms sum to at most 2*R. Define W0=-b0(-x). Apply E002 with Q=T,theta=0,B0=2*R to U0,W0. Their zero mean, reality and norm sum are unchanged by reflection; theta=0 lies in (-1,0]. Its source common untwisting multiplier is an L^2 isometry, so E002 and reflection give sup||u_a0-u_b0||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. This includes the original H^gamma ball since each norm is <=R. Discharge L2. The constructions and bounds hold for every chosen datum; M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A. This proves N001.

argument.text: Fix tau>0, alpha,beta real. If either phase vanishes its exponential is 1 and the covariance is zero. In the remaining case assume L1: alpha*beta!=0. Define h(s)=exp(-i*alpha*s)-Mavg_tau(exp(-i*alpha*.)). Then eta=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau h(s)exp(-i*beta*s)ds. The elementary integral estimate |exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r)|<=|alpha||s-r| gives |h(s)|<=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau |alpha||s-r|dr<=tau|alpha|. Consequently |eta|<=tau|alpha|. At s=0,tau the sharper integrals are each tau|alpha|/2, so |h(0)|+|h(tau)|<=tau|alpha|; also integral_0^tau|h'(s)|ds=tau|alpha|.

produces.statement: Under L1, |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau|alpha| and |h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral_0^tau|h'|<=2*tau|alpha|.

argument.text: Integration by parts against exp(-i*beta*s), which has nonzero derivative factor -i*beta under L1, gives |eta|<= (|h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral|h'|)/(tau|beta|)<=2|alpha/beta| by F001. The defining covariance is symmetric in alpha,beta; repeating both estimates with the phases interchanged gives |eta|<=tau|beta| and |eta|<=2|beta/alpha|. Take their minima, discharge L1, and include the zero-phase case already calculated. Universal introduction proves N002.

argument.text: For the pointwise assertions fix integers a,b,c,d and assume L1: abcd!=0 and a+b+c+d=0. Order their magnitudes as N1>=N2>=N3>=N4. The largest is bounded by the sum of the other three, so N1<=3*N2. Put A0=|ab|, B0=|cd|. If d is among the two largest, min(A0/B0,B0/A0)<=1 and 1/|d|<=1/N3. If not, the largest two are among a,b,c. If they are a,b, use B0/A0 to bound the desired expression by |c|/|ab|<=1/N3. If they are a,c, their ratio lies in [1/3,3]. Therefore the expression is at most 3*min(|b|/|d|^2,1/|b|)<=3/max(|b|,|d|)=3/N3: use the first alternative if |d|>=|b| and the second otherwise. The case b,c is identical after swapping a,b. This proves the first majorant.

produces.statement: Under L1, N1<=3*N2 and (1/|d|)min(A0/B0,B0/A0)<=3/N3.

argument.text: For the second majorant, if the two largest are in the same pair of (a,b),(c,d), the other pair sums to magnitude at most 2*N3. Since a+b=-(c+d), |a+b|/max(A0,B0)<=2*N3/(N1*N2)<=2/N3. If they lie in different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them, whence max(A0,B0)>=N2*N3; also |a+b|<=2*N1<=6*N2 by F001. The quotient is <=6/N3. Any ordering of ties is covered. Discharge L1; these are the claimed conditional pointwise statements for all such frequencies.

Fix four nonnegative ell^2 sequences x_r. First restrict all of them to finitely many frequencies. Decompose each into shells 2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1), j>=0, and let Xshell_(r,j) be its ell^2 norm there. Fix one of the at most 24 orderings of the four shell indices j1>=j2>=j3>=j4, permuting the sequence labels accordingly. A nonzero zero-sum interaction requires j1-j2<=2, since otherwise the largest magnitude would exceed the sum of the other three. For each fixed pair of the two smaller frequencies, sum the two larger-frequency sequences subject to their prescribed sum. Cauchy-Schwarz, applied to a translated reflection, bounds that sum by their shell ell^2 norm product. A shell contains at most 2^(j+1) integers, so summing each smaller sequence in ell^1 costs at most C*2^(j/2) times its ell^2 norm. Thus the shell contribution without the weight is <=C*2^((j3+j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr). On that shell N3>=2^j3, so the weight leaves C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2).

produces.statement: For every ordered four-shell zero-sum interaction j1>=j2>=j3>=j4, its weighted contribution is <=C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr), and j1-j2 is in {0,1,2}.

argument.text: For each q in {0,1,2}, set j1=J,j2=J-q. Drop the upper restrictions on the smaller shells; nonnegativity increases the sum. F002 bounds the ordered contribution by C*(sum_J Xshell_(1,J)*Xshell_(2,J-q))*(sum_(ell>=m>=0)2^(-(ell-m)/2)*Xshell_(3,ell)*Xshell_(4,m)). The first factor is at most ||Xshell_1||_ell2||Xshell_2||_ell2. Set r=ell-m; for each r the second correlation is at most ||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2 by Cauchy-Schwarz, so the second factor is at most sum_(r>=0)2^(-r/2)||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2=||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2/(1-2^(-1/2)). Shell disjointness identifies each shell-norm ell^2 norm with ||x_r||_ell2. Sum over 24 orderings and three offsets. This proves the finite bound with an absolute constant.

produces.statement: The four-linear bound in N003 holds for finite restrictions with an absolute constant independent of the supports.

argument.text: For arbitrary nonnegative ell^2 sequences restrict all inputs to |k|<=m and apply F003. Their norms are bounded by the full norms. Every finite subset of interactions is included in some such restriction, so the infinite positive sum, defined as the supremum over finite subsums, has the same bound. Restricting to any subset only decreases that nonnegative sum. Together with the pointwise assertions this proves N003 without exchanging conditionally convergent sums.

argument.text: Dualize the Fourier coefficients of Rem against a finitely supported unit ell^2 sequence. After absolute values, use F001 and N003 with x_1(a)=|a|^sigma|hat f_1(a)| and likewise for slots 2 and 3; take x_4(d) to be the modulus of the dual coefficient at -d. Their norms are bounded by the three H^sigma norms and the unit dual norm. The factor exp(-i*t0*Phi) has modulus one, and the prefactor in Rem is tau/18. Thus ||Rem||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma). A multiplier of modulus <=1 only decreases the absolute majorant, so the same proof covers every stated restriction.

argument.text: Approximate each mean-zero H^sigma input by its finite Fourier projections. This defines a unique bounded trilinear extension and retains the inequality. For smooth inputs it coincides with the original absolutely convergent Fourier expression. At sigma=0 this supplies in particular an L^2-by-L^2-by-L^2 bound C*tau.

argument.text: For any mean-zero L^2 f, Cauchy-Schwarz in its Fourier series gives ||Dinv f||_infinity<=(sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2, and coefficient weights give ||Dinv f||_(H^1)<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. For a general H^1 function its mean plus this estimate for its derivative gives ||A0||_infinity<=C||A0||_(H^1). The product rule then gives ||A0*B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). Apply it to S_t Dinv f and S_t Dinv g and use S_t isometric and P contractive to obtain ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. Each assertion is quantified over inputs in its indicated space.

argument.text: For L^2 f,g, every Fourier coefficient of the product (S_t f)(S_t g) has modulus <=||f||_2||g||_2 by Cauchy-Schwarz in the convolution. Hence ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_(k!=0) k^2<k>^(-2*pstar), a finite sum because pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum k^(-2) proves ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1), so ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2. Finally J_t(A0,g) is a product of S_t Dinv A0 in L^2 and S_t Dinv g in L^infinity, followed by contractions, so its L^2 norm is <=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2 by F001. Approximation by polynomials and these continuous bilinear bounds justify the products and their extensions.

argument.text: For the normal-form clause take smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b]. At k!=0 the coefficient of J_t is sum_(r+s=k) exp(-i*t*3*k*r*s)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiating the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients. Therefore d_t J_t(f,g)=3*B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smooth spatial Fourier series and all derivatives used here converge absolutely, so differentiation and integration are legitimate. Integration gives the displayed two-endpoint normal form. For piecewise smooth continuous paths apply this on each subinterval; intermediate J endpoint values cancel because the paths are continuous.

argument.text: Symmetry of J is immediate from the product formula. For constant f,g, integrate F003 and multiply by 1/2 to obtain Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/6)[J_s(f,g)]_a^t. This establishes every identity asserted in N005.

argument.text: Fix a,tau,t,w,M0 and assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. Set wshift=S_a w. It is mean-zero and has the same H^gamma norm. argument.text: Fix tau>0. N005 makes Dinv:L^2->H^1 bounded and H^1 an algebra. Therefore Ftau is a continuous quadratic map L^2->H^1. In Htau the first product has factors S_tau Dinv f and Dinv Ftau(f) in H^1; the second uses the continuous bilinear mean P0(f^2) and S_tau Dinv f; the third is an H^1 cube followed by Dinv and S; the fourth multiplies S_(s-tau)Dinv2 Ftau(f) by S_s Dinv f in H^1, followed by Dinv2 and S, evaluated at two endpoints. Every coefficient, including 1/tau, is finite at this fixed tau. Hence all four terms, Ftau and Psi_tau are continuous in L^2. Fourier conjugate symmetry is preserved by S, Dinv, products and real coefficients. Every projected or inverse-derivative term has zero mean, and the unprojected second term of Htau is a scalar times the mean-zero S_tau Dinv f. Thus the update is real and mean-zero. The same formulas preserve spatial smoothness. Finite induction gives the asserted well-defined finite trajectories and continuous dependence at fixed tau.

Also z=f+F has bounded L^2 norm and z'=F'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), whose H^(-pstar) norm is bounded by N005, so ||z||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

produces.statement: Under L1, ||f||_2<=M0+1, q<=2, the H^1 stage and stage-difference bounds in N008 hold, sup(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, and ||z||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

argument.text: Set Astage=Fstage_(a,t)(w) and Dstage=F-Astage. Apply the product bound in N006 to partial_x(S_t Astage) and S_t Astage, using the H^(1+gamma) and H^(a_gamma) stage bounds. It gives ||partial_x[(S_t Astage)^2]||_2<=2*C_gamma||Astage||_(H^(1+gamma))||Astage||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau^gamma. The difference of squares is (S_t Dstage)*S_t(F+Astage). The H^1 algebra estimate in N005 and F001 give its derivative norm <=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Therefore sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Integrating yields sup||Q||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q. N004 with exponent gamma and the current f,w then bounds Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f) by the same quantity, so ||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup_I||Q||_2+||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: Since Dinv B_t(f,F)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t F)], split f=w+(f-w). N006 bounds the w product by C_gamma||w||_(H^gamma)||F||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q using F001. For the other product use ||f-w||_2||S_t F||_infinity<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta by the uniform H^1 stage bound and N005. Thus sup||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Differentiating the definition Y=Cst+Q-((t-a)/tau)W gives Y'=B_t(f,F)+(1/2)B_t(F,F)-W/tau. N005, F002 and this asymmetric product estimate give sup||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. As Y(a)=0, integration gives sup||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, the Dinv B_t(f,F) bound, the exact Y' formula, sup||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q all hold.

argument.text: Apply the normal form of N005 to Cst=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s))ds, with f constant, F(a)=0 and F'=(1/2)B(f,f). Symmetry and the J(B,h)-to-Ctri identity give exactly Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f). Its J term is O(q) in L^2 by N005 and F001. In its Ctri term use N006 with exponent gamma on (w,w,w) to get O(tau^gamma). Expand the difference from (f,f,f) into three trilinear differences and use N006 with exponent zero on each; their size is O(delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2). Thus sup||Cst||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. With F002 in Y=Cst+Q-affine W this gives sup||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f), and sup_I||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

argument.text: All stage components are mean-zero because B and Rem have zero output mean. N005 gives ||Y'||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv Y'||_2 and ||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv Y||_2. Combine F003 and F004 to obtain ||Y||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q. These constants depend only on gamma and M0; none uses a higher norm of f.

produces.statement: Under L1, ||Y||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup_I||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: Collect F001-F005. Discharge L1 and universally quantify all the step data. This proves every clause of N008.

locals.declaration: Fix a step start a, later a grid starting point for I.
Fix f satisfying the conditional step hypotheses.
Fix w satisfying the conditional step hypotheses.
Use Y from the current step tuple.
Use z from the current step tuple.
Use W from the current step tuple.
Use Vst from the current step tuple.
Define rho by the three integrals/affine term in N009.
Fix an exact twisted path v.
Let V be the interpolation of the smooth numerical trajectory from N007.
Concatenate the step increments rho with initial value zero.

argument.text: First fix a step with the antecedent L1 of N008: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0, delta=||f-w||_2<=1, with smooth real mean-zero f,w, M0>=1 and the stated a,tau. Use its tuple and q. Differentiation of Interp gives Vst'=(1/2)B_t(z,z)-W/tau. Since Vst=z+Y, subtraction of (1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst) gives rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau. The residual increment vanishes at a. N008 bounds ||Y||_2 by C*q, ||z||_2 by C and ||W||_2/tau by C*q, with q<=2. N005 thus gives ||rho'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

produces.statement: Under L1 the differential residual identity holds and ||rho'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

argument.text: For the first integral in rho apply N005's normal form to (Y,z). Its boundary J terms are O(tau*q) using ||Dinv Y||_2<=C*tau*q from N008 and bounded ||z||_2. The integral containing Y' is O(tau*q) by the asymmetric J bound and ||Dinv Y'||_2<=C*q. Since z'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), symmetry turns the remaining term into a fixed multiple of Ctri_[a,t](f,f,Y). Apply N006 with the negative norm on Y: N008 gives ||Y||_X<=C*q and ||Y||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q, while f is constant with L^2 norm <=M0+1. Hence this term too is O(tau*q), even on a partial step.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(a<=t<=a+tau)||integral_a^t B_s(Y,z)ds||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: For integral B(Y,Y), apply the same normal form with Y in both slots. Boundary terms use ||Dinv Y||_2||Y||_2<=C*tau*q^2, and derivative integrals use ||Dinv Y'||_2||Y||_2<=C*q^2 over length tau. Thus it is O(tau*q^2)=O(tau*q) because q<=2. The affine W term is O(tau*q) by N008. Combine with F001-F002 to prove both residual estimates on the whole or any initial part of the step. Discharge L1 and quantify the data.

produces.statement: For every step satisfying the N008 hypotheses, the exact residual identities and both quantitative step bounds in N009 hold.

argument.text: Now fix a smooth numerical trajectory and exact twisted v and assume L2: sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h<=1 and E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2<=1. N007 gives the continuous interpolation V with grid values v^n. Concatenate the residual increments, obtaining Rres and V'=(1/2)B(V,V)+Rres' stepwise and distributionally. At each intersected step start t_n, delta_n=||v^n-v(t_n)||_2=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I, so its q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I and F003 applies with w=v(t_n),f=v^n. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps; the last can be partial. Sum the step increment bounds to obtain sup_I||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). Also sup||Rres'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L2, the accumulated residual bound in N009 holds, and ||Rres'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

argument.text: Under L2, ||v||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0 and ||V||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0+1. Subtract the equations to obtain e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Rres'. N005 and F004 imply ||e'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), so ||e||_X has the same bound. The exact equation bounds ||v'||_(H^(-pstar)), and V=v-e then has bounded X norm too, since tau^gamma+E_I<=2. This proves the remaining assertions. Discharge L2 and quantify the trajectory and interval.

locals.declaration: Fix 0<tau<=1, with the smaller final restriction imposed later.
Fix the exact twisted path v.
Fix the interpolation V of the specified numerical trajectory.
Fix a grid starting point a.
Use the concatenated step residual defined by N009.
Fix an arbitrary proof-only threshold N>=2.
Choose C0>=1 dominating the finite constants in F005, uniformly over admissible intervals and trajectories.

argument.text: Assume L1: the smooth real mean-zero v satisfies v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and the numerical interpolation V is taken on an interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, E_I<=1. Set e=v-V,g=v-e/2 and take the concatenated Rres from N009. Its conclusions apply to this trajectory and give the accumulated residual and X bounds. In particular e'=B_t(e,g)-Rres', so integration gives e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). Also ||e||_X<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||v||_X+||V||_X+||g||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

produces.statement: Under L1 the exact error identity and the residual/X bounds of N009 hold on I; g=v-e/2 has bounded X norm.

argument.text: Fix N>=2 only in the proof. For each time s, the inverse-product bound of N005 and the Fourier inequality ||Ple_N partial_x^2 A||_2<=N^2||A||_2 give ||Ple_N B_s(e,g)||_2<=C*N^2||e||_2||g||_2. Indeed B_s(e,g)=S_(-s)partial_x^2 Dinv P[(S_s e)(S_s g)]. Integrate over length at most h and use bounded ||g||_2 to obtain sup||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, for every N>=2, sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

argument.text: Apply the two-endpoint normal form N005 to F_I. The equations give e'=B(e,g)-Rres' and g'=(1/2)B(v,v)-(1/2)B(e,g)+(1/2)Rres'. In the differentiated J terms, its symmetry and integral J(B,h)=Ctri give Ctri(e,g,g)-(1/2)Ctri(e,g,e)=Ctri(e,g,V), since g-e/2=V. The other cubic term is (1/2)Ctri(v,v,e), and the forcing terms satisfy -J(Rres',g)+(1/2)J(e,Rres')=-J(Rres',V). Multiplication by -1/3 yields F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. Both endpoints are retained. Apply the H^1 bound for J in N005: their projections above N are <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I. Continuity of all the paths makes internal endpoints cancel when the normal form is applied stepwise.

produces.statement: Under L1, the full normal-form identity in N010 holds and its two endpoint contributions above N have norm <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I.

argument.text: For any three admissible paths on I, put Lproj=Ple_(N/3),Hproj=I-Lproj. The telescoping expansion Ctri(f_1,f_2,f_3)-Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Lproj f_3)=Ctri(Hproj f_1,f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Hproj f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Hproj f_3) places a high input in each term. The all-low term has no output above N because all product frequencies sum. Each projection contracts both components of X and ||Hproj f_i||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||f_i||_2 by Fourier weights. Apply N006 with the negative norm on that particular high slot. This proves ||Pgt_N Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product_j||f_j||_(L^infinity L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e), using F001: their total contribution is <=C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1 the two cubic terms in F003, projected above N, are bounded by C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I; the general high-output trilinear inequality proved here holds for all admissible paths.

argument.text: For the remaining integral in F003 substitute the actual stepwise Rres' formula from N009, and use integral J(B,h)=Ctri from N005 on each intersected step segment. It becomes -Ctri(Y_n,z_n,V)-(1/2)Ctri(Y_n,Y_n,V)-tau^(-1)integral J_s(W_n,V)ds. At that step's start, delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. N008 gives ||Y_n||_X<=C*q_n, ||Y_n||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C and ||W_n||_2<=C*tau*q_n. N006, with the negative norm on Y_n, bounds the first two terms by C*tau*q_n (using q_n<=2 and ||V||_X<=C from F001). The last term is also <=C*tau*q_n by the L^2 J bound from N005. These remain valid upper bounds on a partial final step. At most h/tau+1 steps are met, and q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I. Thus the forcing integral is bounded by C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L1 the forcing bound in S005, the endpoint bound F003, the cubic bound F004, the low-frequency bound F002 and the residual bound F001 all have constants that can be dominated by a single C0>=1 depending only on gamma,M0, uniformly in N>=2, admissible intervals, trajectories, timesteps and higher norms.

argument.text: Combine F003-F005 to obtain sup||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. With F002, the exact error identity and residual bound in F001 give E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. All constants are uniform in the parameters specified in F005.

produces.statement: Under L1 the high-frequency and final absorbable inequalities stated in N010 hold with one constant depending only on gamma,M0.

argument.text: Choose C0>=1 dominating these constants from F005-F006, independently of all the particular paths. Define N0=ceil(max(2,16*C0,(16*C0)^(1/pstar))). Then C0*(N0^(-1)+N0^(-pstar))<=1/8<=1/4. Put delta0=min(1,1/(8*C0*(N0^2+3))) and K0=4*C0. If h<=delta0 and tau<=delta0/2, then C0*(N0^2*h+h+tau)<=C0*delta0*(N0^2+3)<=1/8<=1/4. F006 therefore has E_I coefficient at most 1/2. Absorption gives E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+2*C0*(h+tau)*tau^gamma<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. These choices depend only on gamma,M0. Discharge L1, retaining its antecedents in the conditional theorem, and quantify all trajectories, intervals and timesteps. This proves N010.

locals.declaration: Choose a uniform flow bound A from F001.
Choose the common stability length delta0 from F002.
Choose K0 together with delta0 from F002.
Put tau=T/Lsteps under the positive-integer antecedent.
Take the unique exact flow for u_0 from N001 under L1.
Use the numerical interpolation from N007 with initial datum u_0.

argument.text: H001-H003 give T>0,0<gamma<=1,R>0. N001 supplies a finite uniform H^gamma bound A(T,gamma,R) for the exact flow over this entire ball; enlarging it to a nonnegative value is harmless. In particular, record F001: there exists such an A, simultaneously valid for all data in the ball, and smooth data have smooth exact flows.

produces.statement: There exists A>=0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that every datum in the original ball has exact-flow H^gamma bound A on [0,T], with smooth flows for smooth data.

argument.text: Choose A from F001 and set M0=1+A. Apply N010 with this M0 and the fixed gamma. Its quantitative choices depend only on gamma,M0, so there exist common delta0 in (0,1] and K0>0 for the whole initial-data ball, not for one numerical trajectory. Record this existence as F002.

produces.statement: There exist delta0 in (0,1] and K0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that the conditional local stability bound of N010 holds for every exact and numerical path under this common bound M0.

argument.text: Choose delta0,K0 together from F002. Put Bcount=ceil(2*T/delta0)+1, Csm=K0*delta0*(2^Bcount-1), and tausm=min(1,delta0/2,(1/(4*(Csm+1)))^(1/gamma)). These are positive and depend only on T,gamma,R; for tau<=tausm, Csm*tau^gamma<1/4. These choices precede the choice of data and number of steps.

produces.statement: Csm>0,tausm>0 depend only on T,gamma,R, tausm<=min(1,delta0/2), and Csm*tau^gamma<1/4 whenever 0<tau<=tausm.

argument.text: Fix u_0,Lsteps and assume L1: u_0 is smooth, real and mean-zero, ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R, Lsteps is a positive integer, and tau=T/Lsteps<=tausm. Let u be its N001 flow, v=S_(-t)u and V the N007 interpolation of the smooth numerical trajectory; e=v-V is continuous and e(0)=0. The common bound is sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=A<M0 and v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Put mblock=floor(delta0/tau). Since tau<=delta0/2, mblock>=1 and mblock*tau is in [delta0/2,delta0]. Divide the grid into blocks of mblock steps, with a possibly shorter final block. There are at most Bcount blocks. On each block, or its initial part, on which the bootstrap sup||e||_2<=1 holds, F002 and N010 give E_block<=2||e(start)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. Induction from e(0)=0 yields E on block j at most K0*delta0*(2^j-1)*tau^gamma, and hence <=Csm*tau^gamma, as long as the bootstrap is valid. A block truncated inside a step is covered by N010.

produces.statement: Under L1, on every initial interval where sup||e||_2<=1 the complete block induction gives sup||e||_2<=Csm*tau^gamma<1/4, including a final endpoint inside a step.

argument.text: Suppose L2: ||e||_2 reaches 1 somewhere on [0,T]. By continuity and e(0)=0 there is a first such time; the bootstrap is valid up to it. F004, with the last block truncated at that time, gives a bound <1/4, a contradiction. Discharge L2 by classical contradiction. Thus the bootstrap never fails and F004 holds on all [0,T]. N007 gives V(n*tau)=S_(-n*tau)u^n, and S_(n*tau) is unitary, so the grid norm ||e(n*tau)||_2 equals ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2. Discharge L1 and quantify u_0,Lsteps. The constants were chosen first, uniformly, so both full assertions of N011 follow.

locals.declaration: Choose C=Csm from the common smooth bound F001.
Choose tau_0=tausm together with C from F001.
Take the exact solution of N001 for the current u_0 under L1.
useq_m is the unique N001 flow for u0seq_m.
unumseq_m is the Psi_tau recursion with datum u0seq_m.

argument.text: H001-H003 fix precisely T>0,0<gamma<=1,R>0. N011 supplies constants Csm,tausm valid simultaneously for every smooth real mean-zero datum in this H^gamma ball and every allowed number of steps. Record F001: such a common positive pair exists, depending only on T,gamma,R.

produces.statement: There exist C>0,tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that the grid bound C*tau^gamma holds for every smooth real mean-zero datum with H^gamma norm <=R and every positive Lsteps with tau=T/Lsteps<=tau_0.

argument.text: Choose that common pair C,tau_0 before fixing arbitrary u_0,Lsteps. Assume L1: u_0 is real, mean-zero, in H^gamma with norm <=R, Lsteps is a positive integer and tau=T/Lsteps<=tau_0. Since T>0, this tau is positive. N001 supplies its unique exact solution u with the stipulated smooth-approximation meaning. Define u0seq_m=Ple_m u_0. Each is a real mean-zero trigonometric polynomial, its H^gamma norm is <=R, and ||u0seq_m-u_0||_2 tends to zero by convergence of the Fourier norm tails. Thus F001 applies to every approximating datum with exactly these C,tau_0.

produces.statement: Under L1, u0seq_m is smooth real mean-zero, has H^gamma norm <=R, converges to u_0 in L^2, and the same C,tau_0 smooth grid estimate applies for every m.

argument.text: Let useq_m be the exact flows and unumseq_m their numerical trajectories. N001's L^2 continuous dependence, since the initial L^2 norms sum to <=2*R, gives sup_[0,T]||useq_m-u||_2<=K(T,2*R)||u0seq_m-u_0||_2 ->0. For this fixed tau and finite Lsteps, N007 makes every iterate of the unmodified update continuous on real mean-zero L^2. Inducting over n=0,...,Lsteps gives unumseq_m^n -> u^n in L^2 at every grid point. No uniform Lipschitz bound for Psi as tau->0 is required: the limit is taken at a fixed timestep, with finite 1/tau coefficients and finitely many iterations.

produces.statement: Under L1, useq_m -> u uniformly in L^2 on [0,T], and unumseq_m^n -> u^n in L^2 at every one of the finitely many grid points.

argument.text: For each m, F002 yields max_n||useq_m(n*tau)-unumseq_m^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. Use F003 and continuity of the norm, and then take the maximum over the finite Lsteps+1 points, to pass to the limit. This gives max_n||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. The exact solution is the unique smooth-approximation solution by N001; N007 ensures the rough-data recursion is defined and stays real mean-zero. The constants C,tau_0 are unchanged in this limit and were chosen uniformly before u_0,Lsteps. Discharge L1 and introduce both universal quantifiers. P follows for the entire original ball, with no Fourier support or extra smoothness hypothesis.
